(Today through Saturday)...
Issued at 131 AM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

Today Through Monday.

The synoptic setup features a weakening mid-level trough associated 
with the remnants of Isaias exiting to the east with lingering mid-
level moist advection and weak surface frontogenesis across 
southeastern central Indiana. HREF component members including the 
HRRR and NAM3km show remnant light rain and low-level cloudiness 
ending west to east between 12Z and 16Z as subsidence behind the 
trough axis takes hold. Deepening boundary layer mixing under weak 
northwest surface flow behind the departing surface boundary will 
clear cloud cover by mid-afternoon. Thermal profiles off the GFS and 
ECMWF show 850 MB temperatures near 10C to 12C, supporting daytime 
highs in the low to mid 70s across the CWA. Surface high pressure 
centered over the Ohio Valley will maintain light and variable winds 
overnight, allowing radiational cooling to drop surface temperatures 
into the mid 50s. Fog looks likely across eastern Indiana tonight
as the clearing reaches the area and winds drop to near calm. The
western extent of the fog remains uncertain and will depend on 
the timing of the clearing.

In the aftermath of the exiting low, a surface high will slide east 
toward the Mid-Atlantic coast on Monday as a broad trough amplifies 
across the Northern Plains. Surface pressure falls across the Upper 
Midwest will tighten the regional pressure gradient, strengthening 
low-level southerly to southwesterly return flow. Deterministic GFS 
and ECMWF soundings display a deep boundary layer with winds at the 
top around 20-25kt. Model guidance shows dry mid-level air beneath 
deep subsidence, which will allow for RH values to drop to around 40 
to 50 percent. With this strong WAA and clouds limited to high 
cirrus, much above normal temperatures are expected with some spots 
near the Illinois border reaching close to 90 degrees. Gusty 
southwesterly winds of 15 to 25 mph are expected during the 
afternoon hours before relaxing slightly Monday night as the 
boundary layer decouples under mostly clear skies. 

Tuesday Through Saturday.

The unseasonably warm thermal ridge will remain positioned across 
the Ohio Valley on Tuesday ahead of a potent cold front extending 
from an upper-level low moving across Ontario and the Upper Great 
Lakes. Models continue to show good agreement in high temperatures 
climbing into the upper 80s under mostly sunny skies with another 
day of deep boundary layer mixing. Moisture transport will begin to 
ramp up late Tuesday night along the pre-frontal trough axis as a 40 
kt LLJ advects Gulf moisture, increasing PWATs above 1.3 inches. 
Scattered shower activity will enter northwestern counties after 06Z 
Wednesday.

Model guidance, including deterministic runs and ensemble clusters 
from the GEFS and EPS, shows the surface cold front decelerating and 
stalling west-to-east across central Indiana Wednesday and Thursday 
as it becomes parallel to the mid-level atmospheric flow. Strong 
lower-level baroclinic forcing combined with broad synoptic lift 
from an approaching shortwave trough will generate widespread 
precipitation along and south of the boundary. Soundings show modest 
MUCAPE between 300-800 J/kg along with 0-6 km bulk shear exceeding 
40 kt, supporting embedded elevated convection and isolated heavier 
rainfall totals. While models have a good idea on the broader 
synoptic pattern, there remains quite a bit of uncertainty as to the 
phasing of the system and where the stronger forcing sets up which 
keeps confidence low on precipitation totals.

The upper trough axis clears the region early Friday, driving the 
frontal boundary well south into the Tennessee Valley and opening 
the door for strong post-frontal CAA. Surface high pressure of 
Canadian origin will build southeastward from the Northern Plains 
into the Great Lakes and Ohio Valley. Gusty northwesterly winds 
Friday morning will gradually diminish by Saturday as the core of 
the high centers over the region. High temperatures on Friday will 
reach the upper 60s, cooling further on Saturday to the upper 50s.
Clear skies and light winds Friday night and Saturday night will 
promote efficient radiational cooling, dropping overnight lows 
into the upper 30s to lower 40s across central Indiana with frost 
looking increasingly likely along with a potential freeze in more 
rural and typically cooler areas.
